About Turn




Turn is a venture-backed B2B software company built for the realities of high-volume hiring. Our platform runs pre-employment background checks and continuous monitoring, and integrates directly into the systems employers already hire with — so teams in hospitality, staffing, construction, healthcare, and real estate can screen candidates fast without giving up compliance. We’re a small, fully remote team that moves quickly and ships real things.  





About the Role




We’re looking for a hands-on Growth Marketing Engineer to own our full-funnel demand engine and turn the traffic and buying signals we already generate into qualified demos and pipeline.  




You’ll sit at the intersection of performance marketing, marketing operations, conversion optimization, and analytics, building and running the systems that move a prospect from first touch to booked meeting. This is a builder’s role: you’ll spend your days in the ad platforms, the CRM, the analytics tools, and the page builder, shipping changes and measuring their impact on qualified-demo volume and pipeline.  




What You’ll Do




Paid acquisition: Plan, launch, and optimize paid campaigns (Google Ads — Performance Max and Search, LinkedIn), architecting campaign structure, audience targeting, and conversion-event mapping so spend optimizes toward booked demos and pipeline rather than clicks, with clean, server-imported conversion tracking (enhanced/offline conversions from the CRM).


Conversion rate optimization: Build and A/B test dedicated demo landing pages, landing pages, forms, and CTAs that turn visitors into meetings, including persona-aware routing (buyer vs. candidate vs. partner) across the site, and own the on-site demo path.


Marketing operations & RevOps: Own the full lead lifecycle and the automation behind it — CRM workflows, lifecycle-stage instrumentation, lead scoring and routing, and the visitor-signal-to-outbound engine across HubSpot, Amplemarket, RB2B, Duo, and Zapier. Build and scale the loop that turns identified in-market website visitors into timely, signal-based 1:1 outreach.


Email deliverability & infrastructure: Own outbound sending infrastructure — mailbox and domain strategy, warm-up and rotation, pre-send verification, and deliverability health — so outreach lands in the inbox and protects the primary domain’s reputation.


Analytics & reporting: Build and own the measurement layer end to end — define the key conversion events, GA4, UTM governance, conversion validation — and build the dashboards that tie marketing activity to pipeline and revenue (Mode).


Conversion copywriting: Write the ad, landing-page, and signal-based outbound copy that drives response.









What You’ll Need




Hands-on experience across growth marketing, demand generation, marketing operations, or revenue operations — ideally in B2B SaaS. You’re a builder who works inside the tools, not only a strategist.


Real performance-marketing experience, especially Google Ads (including Performance Max and Search campaign structure), with a habit of optimizing toward CAC and pipeline instead of vanity metrics.


Fluency with a modern marketing / CRM automation stack (we use HubSpot, Amplemarket, RB2B, Intercom, Zapier, and Calendly; comparable tools like Salesforce, Marketo, or Make are fine).


Analytics chops: GA4, disciplined UTM and conversion tracking, and enough SQL / BI to build your own dashboards (we use Mode; Looker, Amplitude, or similar is fine).


CRO instincts and conversion copywriting ability.


A data-driven, experimental, self-directed way of working — you read the funnel, ship the fix, and measure the result.


Bilingual Spanish/English, with fluent written English.









This is our ideal profile, not a checklist. If you can do the work, we’d love to hear from you regardless of years or title.

About Zenit Corp

Zenit Corp is a fast growing ecommerce group that owns and operates multiple DTC brands across different markets.

Role

The Creative Strategist is responsible for connecting marketing performance with creative execution. This person turns research, data, customer psychology, and business priorities into clear creative direction for paid social, landing pages, campaign concepts, and content tests.

This role is not limited to coming up with ideas. The Creative Strategist is responsible for building a structured creative process, identifying winning angles, writing strong creative briefs, analyzing what is working, and helping the team produce ads designed to perform.

This person works directly with the Head Of Marketing and marketing team, and collaborates with media buyers, designers, editors, copywriters, and creators to make sure creative output is aligned with growth objectives.

The role is expected to bring taste, structure, speed, and performance oriented thinking to a growing ecommerce group.




Creative Strategist Responsibilities




❖ Creative Strategy & Research

➢ Research customers, competitors, market trends, ad libraries, reviews, comments, and social platforms to identify strong creative opportunities.

➢ Translate customer motivations, objections, desires, and buying triggers into creative angles, hooks, messages, and offers.

➢ Build a clear understanding of each brand’s positioning and customer psychology.

➢ Stay close to what is working across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, and other relevant platforms.




❖ Ad Concepts, Hooks & Creative Briefs

➢ Develop new ad concepts, hooks, scripts, storyboards, UGC directions, landing page ideas, and campaign angles.

➢ Write clear creative briefs that explain the objective, target customer, key message, structure, examples, and success criteria.

➢ Create both quick iterations and bigger creative tests that can help unlock new performance.

➢ Maintain an organized backlog of creative tests, angles, and hypotheses for each brand.




❖ Performance Analysis & Creative Testing

➢ Analyze creative performance with the marketing team to understand what drives clicks, conversions, CPA, ROAS, retention, and scale.

➢ Identify patterns in winning and losing creatives and turn those patterns into new tests.

➢ Help define creative testing roadmaps and prioritize the ideas most likely to improve performance.

➢ Create feedback loops between performance results and future creative production.




❖ Collaboration With Creative Production

➢ Work closely with designers, editors, copywriters, media buyers, creators, and other team members to turn ideas into finished assets.

➢ Give clear, practical, and constructive feedback on creative work.

➢ Make sure creative assets are aligned with the brief, the brand, the customer insight, and the performance goal.

➢ Build repeatable frameworks, references, and standards that help the team produce better creative over time.




❖ Brand, Customer & Market Understanding

➢ Protect each brand’s positioning while still pushing for strong direct response performance.

➢ Use customer language to improve ads, landing pages, hooks, and messages.

➢ Identify new angles based on customer objections, product benefits, competitive gaps, and market shifts.

➢ Help the company build a stronger creative foundation as the group grows.




What This Role Is Not

➢ This role is not a traditional Creative Director role focused only on visual taste or brand aesthetics.

➢ This role is not a graphic designer, video editor, or content creator role, although it works closely with those functions.

➢ This role is not responsible for managing ad spend or making final media buying decisions alone.

➢ This role is not a pure social media management or community management role.

➢ This role is not responsible for defining company strategy on its own.

➢ This role is not about producing random ideas without research, structure, testing, or performance accountability.




The Creative Strategist owns creative research, angles, briefs, testing direction, performance learning, and creative feedback loops. The Head Of Marketing and marketing leadership own final business priorities, budgets, and strategic decisions.




Compensation & Benefits

➢ Compensation package of up to 25k USD including bonus, depending on experience, scope of responsibility, and performance.

➢ Opportunity to play a key role inside a rapidly growing ecommerce group.

➢ Direct exposure to company strategy, performance marketing, creative production, and brand growth.

➢ High ownership over the creation of the group’s creative strategy function.

➢ Clear path toward becoming a key creative and growth leader within a multi brand ecommerce group.

➢ Additional performance bonuses for working ads: when a concept, hook, script, or creative brief becomes a strong performing ad and materially helps improve results, the role can receive extra upside tied to that impact.




Ideal Candidate

➢ Strong creative strategy profile with the ability to connect customer insight, storytelling, and performance data.

➢ Comfortable working directly with a founder led leadership team.

➢ Able to create clear, useful, and execution oriented creative briefs.

➢ Strong understanding of paid social creative, direct response marketing, customer psychology, hooks, angles, offers, and creative testing.

➢ Comfortable analyzing ad performance and translating data into practical creative improvements.

➢ Strong written communication and copywriting ability.

➢ Highly organized, reliable, and comfortable building systems from scratch in a fast moving company.

➢ Ambitious and comfortable operating in a fast paced, high growth environment.

➢ Previous experience in ecommerce, DTC brands, performance marketing, paid social, creative strategy, UGC, advertising, copywriting, or growth teams is highly valued.

AI Strategist Consultant

Role Overview

The AI Strategist Consultant works with clients after they sign, turning their business problems into AI solutions that get built and used. You sit between the client's team and ours. You learn how their business runs, find where AI can save time or money, scope the work, and build early prototypes yourself with tools like Claude, ChatGPT and Claude Code. A Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) from our team builds most of the final solution, and you work with them from the first call to launch. You also pay close attention to what the client struggles with outside the current project. Those pain points often lead to the next engagement, so spotting them is a core part of the job. You report to the Head of Operations.




Key Responsibilities

Discovery and Pain Point Identification

Run working sessions with client teams to understand how their business operates today and where time, money or quality is lost.

Spot problems the client has not asked us to solve yet, and write them up clearly with the business case behind each one.

Bring those opportunities to the Head of Operations and the sales team so we can follow up with a proposal.

Rank AI opportunities by business value, effort and risk, and help the client choose what to do first.




AI Strategy and Scoping

Turn each opportunity into a clear scope with goals, success measures, data needs and a delivery plan.

Build AI roadmaps that show the client what to do now, next and later.

Explain what AI can and cannot do today, in plain business language, including where a person should stay in the loop.

Estimate the return on each solution (hours saved, cost reduced, revenue added) before and after we build it.




Prototyping and Delivery

Build quick prototypes and proofs of concept with Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools to test an idea before the team commits to building it.

Work side by side with the FDE on the engagement. You define the problem and the outcome, and the FDE builds the production solution.

Review what the team builds against the original goals, and catch gaps early.

Keep every engagement on schedule and flag risks to the Head of Operations before they become problems.




Adoption and Training

Teach client teams how to use what we deliver, through workshops, walkthroughs and short guides.

Track whether people actually use the solution after launch, and fix what gets in the way.

Collect client feedback and share what you learn with our delivery and engineering teams.




Client Communication

Serve as a trusted advisor for client leadership and day to day teams.

Present findings, roadmaps and results to executives in clear, direct language.

Travel to the US/MX for on-site workshops, kickoffs and client meetings when the engagement calls for it.




Requirements




Experience

2 to 3 years of consulting experience.

Experience running discovery sessions, workshops and interviews with client teams.

A track record of finding business problems and turning them into scoped, funded projects.

Proof that you use AI every day to solve real problems. During the interview process, you will show us a real workflow you built with AI.




Skills

Fluent English and Spanish, written and spoken.

Based in Latin America, and able to travel to the US.

Strong business sense. You understand how companies make and lose money, and you can tie an AI idea to a number.

Comfortable with Claude, ChatGPT and other AI tools, and willing to earn certifications on both platforms.

Clear thinking and clear writing. You can explain a complicated idea to a busy executive in a few sentences.

Curious and fast to learn. You keep up with new AI tools and test them on real work.
